The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to move quickly on foot.

draft.emotion: energetic and active, catching your breath after moving fast
notes: Irregular verb: present 'je cours, tu cours, il court, nous courons, vous courez, ils courent'; past participle 'couru' (with 'avoir'); future stem 'courr-' (je courrai).

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, faster than walking, including for exercise.

examples.text: Il doit courir pour attraper le bus.
examples.translation: He has to run to catch the bus.
examples.emotion: urgent and slightly stressed, watching the bus pull away

senses.definition: To hurry from one task or place to another because one has little time.

examples.text: Je cours toute la journée entre le travail et les courses.
examples.translation: I rush around all day between work and errands.
examples.emotion: exhausted and overwhelmed, describing a busy schedule

draftBefore.shortGloss: to run; to race; to rush
draftBefore.emotion: energetic and active, catching your breath after moving fast
notes: While 'courir' is the general word for running, avoid using it to mean 'jogging' in a exercise context. For exercise, French speakers often use the phrase 'faire du jogging'.
